text: The study by Andrade (doodling) was a laboratory experiment. One feature of a laboratory
experiment is that it has controls to limit the effect of extraneous variables.

parts.text: Explain what makes this a ‘non-directional hypothesis’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Write a null hypothesis for this study.

text: A study has the experimental hypothesis ‘There will be a gender difference in aggression’. This is
a non-directional hypothesis rather than a directional hypothesis.

parts.text: Explain one advantage of using one participant in this study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one disadvantage of using one participant in this study.

text: In the study by Pepperberg (parrot learning), Alex the parrot was the only participant.
State two features of a normal distribution.
In the study by Yamamoto et al. (chimpanzee helping), the results included how often the helper’s
first tool offer was a stick. The percentage of stick offers when a stick was needed and when a
straw was needed could be displayed on a bar chart.
Explain why a bar chart would be the most appropriate way to display these results.
Describe ‘opportunity sampling’ and ‘random sampling’, using any examples.
Section B
Answer all questions in this section.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest one behaviour in dreams that Clark could ask about which can be done in
everyday life. Your suggestion must be ethical.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one behaviour in dreams that Clark could ask about which cannot be done in
everyday life. Your suggestion must be ethical.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Clark believes that some participants may lie. For example, they may falsely report dream
behaviours to impress Clark.
Suggest one way that Clark could minimise this type of lying in his study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Clark is concerned that some participants may also lie about their dreams because the events
in them are too personal to report to Clark.
Explain which ethical guideline Clark is concerned about.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Clark thinks that participants’ eye movements during dream sleep are related to the content
of their dreams.
Suggest how Clark could use participants’ eye movements during dream sleep to investigate
whether they are lying about their dream content.

text: Clark is a psychologist investigating whether the behaviours people dream about can be done in
everyday life or not. He is monitoring participants’ sleep in his laboratory and then interviewing
them.

parts.text: Explain whether Liang is conducting a participant observation or a non-participant observation.

Liang expects that if a person has an animal with them, other people will be more likely to say
hello.
Explain one other factor for Liang to observe that could affect whether a person says hello.
Do not refer to age or gender in your answer.

text: Liang is planning to observe behaviour in a park. He is going to sit on a bench and pretend to be
using his phone. His aim is to investigate factors which could cause one person to say hello to
another person. Two possible factors are age and gender.

Section C
Answer all questions in this section.

text: Tara can measure physical reaction time using a machine that records the time between a light
flashing and the participant pressing a button. Tara will use this measurement to investigate
whether there is a relationship between participants’ physical reaction time and how quickly they
can recall numbers.

parts.text:
Describe how Justin could conduct a study using a questionnaire to investigate how different
sports affect adults’ happiness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.

different sports could affect happiness in different ways.
